title: Customer Letter
summary: Apple released a public letter explaining its opposition to a U.S. government demand to build a "backdoor" into the iPhone for the San Bernardino investigation. The company argues that creating such a tool would compromise the security of all iPhone users, set a dangerous precedent, and weaken encryption that protects personal data from hackers and criminals. Apple emphasizes its commitment to safeguarding customer privacy and states that acceding to the government's request would undermine decades of security advancements.

title: IPhone Pro models scarce in stores this holiday - Best Buy
summary: Best Buy announced that higher-end iPhone 14 Pro models will be in short supply this holiday season due to production issues caused by China's zero-COVID policy. This scarcity is expected to negatively impact sales for both Best Buy and Apple during the crucial Black Friday and holiday shopping period, potentially pushing some sales into the next quarter. Despite strong demand for premium smartphones, analysts estimate a significant drop in iPhone sales compared to the previous year.

title: This Growth ETF Continues Winning
summary: The article discusses the continued outperformance of growth stocks over value stocks in early 2020, driven by technology and consumer discretionary sectors. It highlights the SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 Growth ETF (SPYG) as a strong performer, noting its impressive year-to-date gains compared to the broader S&P 500 and S&P 500 Value Index. The piece also contrasts growth and value investing strategies and mentions significant inflows into SPYG.

title: How Microsoft secures its spot among the world's most valuable brands
summary: Microsoft has become one of the world's most valuable brands, with its brand value reaching $661 billion in 2022, securing the number four spot in Kantar BrandZ Most Valuable Global Brands. The company's success is attributed to its meaningful, different, and salient offerings, including superior cloud, software, and hardware products, as well as its commitment to sustainability. Under CEO Satya Nadella, Microsoft has focused on specific market segments, leading to a tenfold increase in brand value and solidifying its position as the world's most valuable business services brand, further boosted by the continued digital transformation and remote work trends.

title: Apple iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max Might Stick To Physical Instead Of Solid State Buttons
summary: Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reports that the iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max will likely retain physical buttons instead of moving to solid-state buttons due to unresolved technical challenges. This change might negatively impact Taptic Engine component suppliers like Cirrus Logic and AAC Technologies. However, it is not expected to delay mass production or shipments, and the solid-state button concept may be pushed to the iPhone 16 series.

title: Union groups, investors seek worker rights review at Apple
summary: Labor groups and investors have filed a shareholder proposal requesting Apple Inc. to review its worker rights practices, citing a potential "misalignment" between Apple's public commitments and alleged anti-union activities. This proposal comes amidst growing unionization efforts at Apple retail stores and builds on previous successful shareholder resolutions concerning civil rights audits and non-disclosure agreements.

title: Apple worth more than US stock index’s energy sector
summary: Apple's market capitalization has surged to nearly $1.2 trillion, surpassing the entire S&P 500 energy sector. This growth is attributed to a strong share rally and the success of its wearables division, contrasting with the struggles of the energy sector due to stagnant oil prices and investor concerns over climate-unfriendly industries.

title: Why did Emerson Network Power rebrand itself as Vertiv?
summary: Emerson Network Power rebranded as Vertiv in January 2017, following its sale by Emerson Electric Co. to Platinum Equity. This transition to a privately-held company allows Vertiv greater flexibility in business strategy, investment decisions, and the ability to focus on long-term growth as a standalone entity. Vertiv aims to capitalize on growth opportunities in Southeast Asia, particularly in cloud computing, data centers, and advanced network infrastructure.

title: Why Markets Think Trump Tariffs Will Help Apple and Hurt Amazon
summary: This article explores why markets believe tariffs will impact Apple positively and Amazon negatively. It highlights Apple's strong embedded position within the Chinese economy, suggesting that China needs Apple as much, if not more, than Apple needs China, thus incentivizing protection from tariffs. Conversely, Amazon's business model, heavily reliant on Chinese-made goods without a similar indispensable role in China's economy, makes it vulnerable to tariff impacts.

title: Apple Updates MacBook Air and MacBook Pro
summary: Apple announced updates to its MacBook Air and MacBook Pro lines, adding True Tone display technology to the MacBook Air and upgrading the entry-level 13-inch MacBook Pro with faster processors and Touch Bar/Touch ID. These updates come with new pricing, including special discounts for university students. The company also announced its Back to School promotion and highlighted features coming with macOS Catalina.

title: Apple Music’s Zane Lowe explains how Spatial Audio will transform music
summary: Zane Lowe, Apple Music's co-head of Artist Relations, discusses the transformative potential of Spatial Audio for both artists and fans. He emphasizes how this new immersive technology, with sound moving in a three-dimensional space, will allow artists to create music in entirely new ways, moving beyond traditional two-channel stereo. Lowe believes Spatial Audio will change how music feels to listeners and foresees future artists growing up creating specifically for this format.

title: Microsoft to cut 7,800 more jobs; writes off $7.6 billion in Nokia deal
summary: Microsoft announced a major restructuring of its mobile devices business, writing off $7.6 billion from its Nokia acquisition and cutting 7,800 jobs globally, primarily in its phone segment. This marks the second round of significant job cuts under CEO Satya Nadella, as the company shifts its strategy from a standalone phone business to growing a vibrant Windows ecosystem. Microsoft aims to narrow its focus to three key customer segments and run a more effective, narrower phone portfolio.

title: Preparing for a world of change: Microsoft’s forward-looking approach to transfer pricing execution and monitoring
summary: This article details how PwC collaborated with Microsoft to overhaul its transfer pricing execution and monitoring processes. Facing complex regulatory environments and business model transformations, Microsoft automated intercompany processes within the SAP platform, established a new Operational Transfer Pricing Team, and integrated PwC's pre-built programs to improve efficiency, reduce risks, and achieve significant benefits in cycle time and audit preparedness.

title: Rackspace Security Incident Causes Thousands To Lose Email Service
summary: Thousands of Rackspace customers lost email service after a security incident caused a weekend-long outage impacting its hosted Exchange. Rackspace began restoring services to Microsoft 365 customers and confirmed the incident was security-related, advising a move to Microsoft 365 for affected users. The incident led to significant customer frustration and a 10 percent drop in Rackspace's stock.

title: Move over Apple, Microsoft now the world’s most valuable company
summary: Microsoft Corp. surpassed Apple Inc. to become the world's most valuable public company after Apple's shares fell due to a $6 billion sales hit from global supply chain issues. Microsoft's stock has surged over 45% this year driven by cloud-based services demand, while Apple, despite robust share buybacks, saw its market capitalization slip below Microsoft's. Both companies face ongoing supply chain challenges, though Microsoft anticipates a strong end to the year for its cloud business.

title: Humanoid Robot Market Demand, Current Outlook, Future Growth,
summary: The humanoid robot market is experiencing significant growth driven by increasing adoption in retail, education, research, and caregiving, as well as technological advancements. Software is expected to dominate the market due to the integration of AI algorithms, while biped motion types also hold a significant share. North America currently leads the market, but the Asia-Pacific region is projected to show the fastest growth.

title: AMD Highlights Future of High-Performance and Adaptive Computing During Opening Keynote of CES 2023
summary: During the CES 2023 opening keynote, AMD Chair and CEO Dr. Lisa Su showcased new leadership products across various markets, emphasizing the role of high-performance and adaptive computing in solving global challenges. AMD unveiled new mobile and desktop processors, including the first x86 PC CPU with a dedicated AI engine and desktop processors with 3D V-Cache technology, alongside new graphics solutions. The company also previewed advancements in AI with the Alveo V70 AI Accelerator and Instinct MI300, and highlighted the use of AMD technology in healthcare and aerospace.

title: DocuSign Wins Award for #1 Mobile Application for Microsoft Office
summary: DocuSign won the Best Mobile App award at Microsoft Ignite 2016 for its eSignature and Digital Transaction Management (DTM) platform's integration with Microsoft Office and SharePoint. This recognition highlights the long-standing strategic partnership between DocuSign and Microsoft, which enables over one billion Microsoft customers to securely sign documents digitally, boosting productivity and compliance. The collaboration has led to significant efficiencies for Microsoft, including eliminating nearly 2 million pieces of paper and achieving faster document completion times.

title: Pentagon awards multibillion-dollar cloud contract to Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle
summary: The Pentagon has awarded a multibillion-dollar cloud computing contract, Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC), to Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Oracle. This move diverges from a previous single-vendor approach (JEDI contract) that faced legal challenges from Amazon alleging interference by former President Trump. The new multi-vendor contract, worth up to $9 billion, aims to provide resilient and cost-effective cloud services for the military, enabling access to sensitive data globally.

title: Sydney Motorway Corp steers the cloud route to strategic success
summary: Sydney Motorway Corporation (SMC) is leveraging cloud and utility computing from its inception for the WestConnex project, Australia's largest transport infrastructure undertaking. By adopting an "as-a-service" model and partnering with Cubesys, SMC's lean IT department focuses on business outcomes, ensuring secure and flexible access to information for its operations and contractors using Microsoft Enterprise Mobility + Security and Office 365, further supported by Azure Active Directory. This approach allows SMC to stay at the forefront of technology while maintaining robust security and user flexibility.

title: Semiconductor stocks are poised to benefit as industry sales growth resumes in 2020
summary: Semiconductor stocks are expected to see a rebound in sales growth in 2020, following a "reset" year in 2019. Despite volatility, these stocks have historically been strong long-term investments. The industry, significantly impacted by U.S.-China trade tensions, anticipates a return to growth with companies like Nvidia projected to see a 17% sales increase next year.

title: BI vendor Phocas raises funds to build predictive analytics
summary: Phocas Software, an Australian-based BI vendor, secured $34 million in venture capital funding to expand its presence, further develop its analytics products, and accelerate growth in the U.S. and U.K. The funding will support the company's move into predictive analytics and new industry verticals. Phocas, which was previously self-funded for 20 years, aims to reach $100 million in revenue.

title: Target Nabs Former Facebook Manager Hari Govind
summary: Target Corp. has appointed Hari Govind, formerly a group manager at Facebook, as its senior vice president of infrastructure and operations for its technology team. In this new role, Govind will oversee digital infrastructure and technology across Target's various operations, leveraging his over two decades of experience to enhance the retailer's technological capabilities. This appointment aligns with Target's ongoing strategy to prioritize digital integration and technology in its business model.

title: ByteDance chooses Oracle over Microsoft for TikTok's US operations
summary: ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese parent company, has selected Oracle as its U.S. technology partner, rejecting Microsoft's bid to acquire TikTok's U.S. operations. This decision comes as the Trump administration threatened to ban TikTok over national security concerns related to its Chinese ownership. Oracle confirmed its joint bid with ByteDance to the Treasury Department.

title: Jaguar Land Rover, Nvidia ally in vehicle software arms race
summary: Luxury automaker Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has partnered with Nvidia to develop advanced computer brains and software for its vehicles launching from 2025 onwards. This collaboration aims to accelerate JLR's in-vehicle software development, enabling features like autonomous driving and parking, and providing more digital functions to drivers. The deal is a significant win for Nvidia in expanding its automotive industry presence and helps JLR compete with rivals like Tesla in digital technology.

title: iShares Russell Top 200 Growth ETF (IWY) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the iShares Russell Top 200 Growth ETF (IWY), covering its stock price, holdings, dividend yield, and key financial statistics. It highlights the ETF's top holdings as of December 31, 2025, which include NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet. The report also details the ETF's performance, asset allocation, and historical data like price-to-earnings and dividend yields.

title: Germany's BioNTech buys British AI startup InstaDeep
summary: BioNTech SE, the German vaccine maker, has acquired British AI startup InstaDeep for up to 562 million pounds ($682 million) to enhance its biotech research and manufacturing capabilities. This acquisition aims to integrate AI into all aspects of BioNTech's work, from target discovery to product delivery. InstaDeep will continue to provide its services to other companies, including Google and Nvidia.

title: Teledyne FLIR Introduces Prism AI, Software for the Development of Automotive Thermal Perception Systems
summary: Teledyne FLIR has introduced Prism AI, a software framework designed to help automotive engineers integrate thermal cameras into advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous vehicle (AV) systems. Prism AI offers features like visible and thermal image fusion, enhancing detection of pedestrians and animals, especially in low-light conditions. This development aims to improve road safety and assist OEMs in meeting upcoming regulatory requirements for nighttime collision prevention.

title: NVIDIA Quadro RTX 6000 Powers World’s Fastest Laptop — ASUS ProArt StudioBook One
summary: NVIDIA announced that the Quadro RTX 6000 GPU will power the ASUS ProArt StudioBook One, hailed as the world's most powerful laptop. This new system joins 11 other RTX Studio systems, bringing the total to 39, and is designed for creative professionals needing high-end workstation performance on the go. The laptop features 24GB of GPU memory, real-time ray tracing, and advanced thermal cooling, supporting demanding workflows like 3D animation, 8K video editing, and VR.

title: Microchip Technology sees record sales as computer chip supply issues persist
summary: Microchip Technology (MCHP) reported record-setting sales at the beginning of its 2022 fiscal year, driven by the ongoing global demand for computer chips. CEO Ganesh Moorthy indicated that the entire semiconductor supply chain remains constrained, suggesting that chip shortages will extend into 2022. The company, based in Chandler, is experiencing strong demand amidst an industry-wide supply crunch.

title: Nvidia Announces GA of AI Enterprise on VMware vSphere and Standard Servers
summary: NVIDIA has announced the general availability of NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a suite of AI tools and frameworks designed to virtualize AI workloads on VMware vSphere and NVIDIA-Certified Systems. This initiative aims to make AI transformative power accessible to a broader range of enterprises by leveraging mainstream data center servers. Several system makers and Domino Data Lab are supporting this launch, with early adopters already utilizing the software in various industries like automotive, education, finance, and healthcare.

title: Nvidia’s GPU cloud for deep learning can now be accessed via Microsoft Azure
summary: Microsoft Corp. has partnered with Nvidia Corp. to enable its Azure cloud customers to utilize Nvidia's GPU Cloud for training deep learning models. This integration provides developers, data scientists, and researchers access to preconfigured containers with GPU-accelerated software, supporting popular deep learning tools like Microsoft’s Cognitive Toolkit, TensorFlow, and PyTorch, and using advanced Nvidia GPUs such as the Tesla V100. The collaboration aims to streamline high-powered computing tasks on Azure, complementing Microsoft's Project Brainwave initiative.

title: $6.5B Texas Instruments Fab Could Be First of Four at Site Totaling $30B
summary: Texas Instruments plans to build up to four semiconductor chip fabrication plants in Sherman, Texas, with the first $6.5 billion fab already under construction and expected to begin production in 2025. The total investment for all four plants could reach nearly $30 billion, supported by significant local incentives. This development is part of a broader U.S. push to increase domestic semiconductor manufacturing amidst global shortages.

title: It’s Time for Ti: NVIDIA Introduces Gaming Flagship — the GeForce RTX 3080 Ti
summary: NVIDIA has announced two new additions to its GeForce RTX family: the GeForce RTX 3080 Ti and GeForce RTX 3070 Ti. The RTX 3080 Ti, launching June 3rd at $1,199, is touted as the new flagship gaming GPU, offering 1.5x faster performance than previous generations and catering to demanding modern games and creative applications. The RTX 3070 Ti, available next week starting at $599, also delivers significant performance improvements over its predecessors.

title: Chinese hacking group ‘Chimera’ targets Taiwanese chip and airline companies
summary: A Chinese advanced threat protection group named "Chimera" is reportedly targeting Taiwanese semiconductor companies to steal intelligence such as IC chip documents, SDKs, IC designs, and source code. Additionally, the group is accused of stealing passenger data from the airline industry, abusing cloud services from Google and Microsoft. Experts suggest these activities, whether state-sponsored or for competitive advantage, highlight a significant cybersecurity threat requiring robust government action.

title: Corsair One i164 SFF PC Review
summary: This review examines the Corsair One i164, a small form factor (SFF) PC featuring an Intel 9900K and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti. The article details its design, I/O, cooling system, and internal specifications, highlighting its quiet operation and powerful components. It assesses whether this new iteration lives up to the high recommendations of its predecessor.

title: Hertz names ex-Goldman finance chief Stephen Scherr as CEO
summary: Hertz Global Holdings has appointed Stephen Scherr, former Goldman Sachs CFO, as its new chief executive officer, effective end of February. Scherr replaces interim CEO Mark Fields and joins Hertz during a pivotal time as the company electrifies its fleet, including a significant deal to acquire 100,000 Tesla vehicles. This leadership change and strategic direction follow Hertz's emergence from bankruptcy and a strong rebound in demand.

title: John Deere’s Electric Concept Tractor Sparks Interest
summary: John Deere plans to unveil a fully electric, high-power tractor, dubbed SESAM, at the Paris International Agribusiness Show. This concept tractor aims to combine classic functionality with the benefits of electricity, offering emissions-free and quiet operation for about four hours on a full charge. While the concept aligns with a broader industry trend towards electric ground transport, a farmer noted potential challenges regarding battery life and charging infrastructure for practical agricultural use.

title: As India waffles on terms for Tesla, several states woo Musk
summary: Several Indian states are inviting Tesla to set up manufacturing facilities in their provinces, following Elon Musk's comments about ongoing challenges with the national government. These states, governed by parties opposed to Prime Minister Modi's administration, are offering incentives like infrastructure and streamlined approval processes. The overtures highlight the ongoing impasse between Tesla and the Indian government over local manufacturing and import duties.

title: Chinese EV maker Li Auto files for US listing
summary: Chinese electric vehicle (EV) maker Li Auto Inc., backed by Meituan Dianping, has filed for a U.S. initial public offering (IPO) on Nasdaq under the symbol "LI". The company, which produces Li ONE extended-range electric SUVs, aims to differentiate itself from rivals like Tesla and Nio by offering vehicles chargeable with both electricity and gasoline. This move follows a surge in share prices for other EV manufacturers and comes as Li Auto expands its showroom presence in China.

title: Tim Draper turns attention from China to Taiwan
summary: US venture capitalist Tim Draper, an early investor in Tesla and SpaceX, has shifted his investment focus from China to Taiwan. He stated that he stopped investing in China due to early signs that it was moving away from a free market under President Xi Jinping, and he now sees Taiwan as a natural place for investment, particularly in its booming tech and semiconductor sector. Draper also expressed concerns about a potential Chinese attack on Taiwan and praised Elon Musk's ability to get things done.

title: GM CEO says making ventilators at Indiana factory changed the company culture
summary: GM CEO Mary Barra states that making ventilators at an Indiana factory during the COVID-19 pandemic significantly changed the company's culture, giving them confidence to accelerate other tasks like electric vehicle development. The experience also influenced GM's approach to securing raw materials for EV production as they transition away from internal combustion engines. Barra also hinted at a potential EV battery factory in Michigan and commented on GM's stock valuation compared to Tesla.

title: Tesla: Tips On When To Go Long
summary: This article provides a technical analysis of Tesla Inc. (TSLA) to identify optimal times for going long. It analyzes various technical indicators like moving averages, price channels, and the Average Directional Index (ADX), along with broader market indicators, to build a long-term bullish bias for TSLA. The report suggests strategies for entering a long position, including aggressive and conservative approaches.

title: Auto parts supplier Aptiv to acquire 85% of Intercable unit in EV tech push
summary: Aptiv Plc announced its acquisition of an 85% stake in Intercable Automotive Solutions for 595 million euros. This strategic move grants Aptiv access to high-voltage busbar technology crucial for electric vehicles and aligns with its broader investments in EV and battery technology. The deal, expected to close by the end of the year, aims to bolster Aptiv's earnings next year and diversify its revenue stream.

title: ElectraMeccanica picks Mesa as site of new Arizona factory to build unusual electric cars
summary: ElectraMeccanica Vehicles Corp. has chosen Mesa, Arizona, as the location for its new assembly and engineering center, which will build its three-wheeled, single-seat SOLO electric cars. The facility is expected to create between 200 and 500 jobs and could produce up to 20,000 vehicles annually. Arizona offered a compelling incentive package and a strong workforce, making it the preferred choice over Tennessee.

title: Ta Win enters into electric vehicle market as subsidiary appointed global vendor
summary: Ta Win Holdings Bhd has expanded into the global electric vehicle (EV) market after its subsidiary, Cyprium Wire Technology Sdn Bhd (CWT), was appointed as a global vendor for Aptiv plc. CWT will use its electron beam irradiation technology to manufacture cables and automotive components for Aptiv, which services 23 of the 25 largest automotive OEMs. This strategic move is expected to open significant growth prospects for Ta Win by leveraging Aptiv's extensive global presence and meeting the increasing demand for EVs.

title: Elon Musk admits Tesla has quality problems
summary: Elon Musk has acknowledged Tesla's quality issues, particularly during new model production ramp-ups, confirming criticisms from engineering consultant Sandy Munro. Munro, who initially criticized the Model 3's quality in 2018, noted significant improvements in later production runs. Musk advised customers to either buy a Tesla at the very beginning of a model's run or once production has stabilized to avoid early quality challenges.

title: General Motors made $6.4 billion in 2020, despite COVID-19
summary: General Motors reported a profit of $6.43 billion in 2020, despite a 4.5% fall from the previous year, driven by strong demand for trucks and SUVs in the latter half of the year. The company is facing new challenges, including an estimated $1.5 billion to $2 billion loss due to a global semiconductor chip shortage in 2021, but anticipates pretax income of $10 billion to $11 billion for the year. GM also unveiled plans to invest over $7 billion in electric and self-driving vehicles in 2021 as part of its broader push into EVs.

title: Apple’s CEO Tim Cook vows to boost Chinese investment amid trade tensions - The News International
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook pledged to increase investment in China during a visit to Beijing, meeting with the Minister of Industry and Information Technology, Li Lecheng. This commitment comes amid US trade tensions and tariffs, highlighting China's crucial role as both a consumer market and manufacturing hub for Apple. Cook also announced the upcoming availability of the iPhone Air in China and reaffirmed Apple's long-term sustainability efforts in the region.

title: Better Stock to Buy Right Now: Apple vs. Amazon - The Globe and Mail
summary: This article compares Apple (AAPL) and Amazon (AMZN), two "Magnificent Seven" stocks, to determine which is a better buy. It highlights Amazon's growing and profitable cloud computing division (AWS) and Apple's high-margin services segment, ultimately recommending Amazon due to the significant growth potential of the cloud computing market.

title: LaCie Introduces New Rugged Mini SSD with Up to 4TB Capacity
summary: LaCie, a brand of Seagate, has introduced the new Rugged Mini SSD, offering up to 4TB of durable, fast, and compact storage for content creators. This portable drive boasts read speeds of up to 2000MB/s with USB 3.2 gen 2x2 technology and features an IP54-rated, 3-meter drop-protected, and 1-ton car pressure-resistant design using recycled materials. It is compatible with a wide range of devices including Apple products and PCs, and comes with a three-year warranty, data recovery services, and a one-month Adobe Creative Cloud All Apps plan.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Apple, Cisco Systems and IBM
summary: This Zacks Analyst Blog highlights recent research reports on Apple Inc. (AAPL), Cisco Systems, Inc. (CSCO), and IBM Corp. (IBM), detailing their recent performance, strategic initiatives, and market outlook. Apple is driven by strong Services growth and iPhone 17, Cisco by its evolving subscription model and Splunk acquisition, while IBM focuses on its Watsonx platform and quantum technology. The article also touches on potential headwinds and opportunities for each company.

title: ARM Skyrockets 17% in a Month: Should You Board the Train? - TradingView
summary: Arm Holdings plc (ARM) shares have surged 17% in the past month due to its mobile market leadership and growing role in AI and IoT despite holding a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). However, concerns are rising due to its heavy dependence on the Chinese market and the increasing adoption of RISC-V, along with high valuation concerns. Investors are advised to wait for a more reasonable entry point despite the compelling long-term story.

title: Prediction: This Unstoppable Vanguard ETF Will Beat the S&P 500 Yet Again in 2026 - Mitrade
summary: The Vanguard Growth ETF (VUG) is predicted to outperform the S&P 500 again in 2026, building on its history of stronger returns since its inception. This is primarily due to its heavier weighting in top-performing technology companies like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Apple, which also dominate the S&P 500. The ongoing artificial intelligence (AI) boom is expected to continue driving growth for these companies and, consequently, for VUG.

title: Here’s why I’d avoid the DGRO ETF and buy VOO instead
summary: The article advises investors to prefer the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) over the iShares Core Dividend Growth ETF (DGRO) for long-term investments. Although DGRO has performed well, VOO has demonstrated superior returns and a lower expense ratio. The author argues that DGRO's low dividend yield makes it less attractive compared to government bonds or other dividend-focused ETFs.

title: Intel (INTC) Stock Surges on Apple Chip Rumors and $208M Malaysia Expansion: 2025 Rally, Analyst Forecasts and What’s Next
summary: Intel (INTC) stock has surged due to rumors of Apple becoming an Intel Foundry customer and a new $208 million expansion in Malaysia. While analysts remain cautious with "Hold" ratings and price targets below current levels, the news validates Intel's 18A process and strengthens its position in global manufacturing and U.S. industrial policy. The company's Q3 2025 results showed early improvements, but challenges remain in foundry execution and competition.

title: Technology Stocks To Watch Now - October 10th - MarketBeat
summary: This article highlights seven technology stocks—NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Meta Platforms, Oracle, Palantir Technologies, and Alibaba Group—identified by MarketBeat's stock screener as having the highest dollar trading volume recently. It provides a brief description of each company and discusses key market trends impacting the tech sector, such as AMD's partnership with OpenAI. The report emphasizes the growth potential and associated risks of investing in technology stocks.

title: How to watch AMD Keynote at CES 2026
summary: AMD CEO Dr. Lisa Su will deliver a keynote address at CES 2026 on Monday, January 5, focusing on the company's vision for future AI solutions. The keynote, which will highlight AMD's role as a major chipmaker and its partnership with OpenAI, is scheduled to start at 9:30 p.m. ET. Viewers can tune into the livestream on YouTube.

title: Apple Prevails In 'Opple' TM Appeal - Law360
summary: A European Union Intellectual Property Office appeals board has ruled in favor of Apple, blocking lighting company Opple from registering a trademark for its name. This decision overturns a previous ruling that suggested a low likelihood of confusion between the two trademarks.

title: Shelton’s New SEPI ETF Looks to Disrupt the Derivative Income Landscape
summary: Shelton Capital has launched the Shelton Equity Premium Income ETF (SEPI), aiming to differentiate itself in the growing derivative income strategy market. The ETF focuses on selling covered calls on individual stocks, leveraging Shelton's nearly two decades of experience in the options space to provide consistent cash flow and manage volatility. This strategy is presented as a way to enhance traditional portfolios and offer reliable income streams in evolving market conditions.

title: DGRW Has Hallmarks of a Great Dividend ETF
summary: The WisdomTree US Quality Dividend Growth Fund (DGRW) is highlighted as a strong dividend ETF due to its focus on companies' return on assets and return on equity, rather than just yield. This strategy has allowed DGRW to outperform the S&P 500 and other dividend indexes, especially in high-interest-rate environments. The ETF's approach aims for reduced volatility, potential capital appreciation, and diversification, including a significant allocation to tech stocks.

title: Microsoft Corporation (MSFT): Among Tiger Global Management’s Long-Term Stock Picks
summary: This article examines Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) as one of Tiger Global Management's long-term stock picks, highlighting its significant presence in the fund's portfolio and strong performance. It discusses Tiger Global's successful public market investments contrasted with its less favorable private market ventures, emphasizing the fund's continued bullish outlook on MSFT amidst the AI boom. Analyst sentiment from UBS also supports a positive outlook for Microsoft.

title: Alphabet’s stock just had its best quarter in two decades thanks to AI
summary: Alphabet's Class A stock experienced its best quarter since 2005, rising 38% in the third quarter of 2025 due to the strong performance of Google’s Gemini and cloud-computing businesses, validating the company's artificial intelligence strategy. Its Class C shares also saw a record-breaking performance, gaining 37%. This growth demonstrates the significant impact of AI on the company's financial results.

title: Microsoft Reportedly Plans to Shift Major New Product Manufacturing Out of CN Starting 2026 - AASTOCKS.com
summary: Microsoft is reportedly planning to move most new product manufacturing, including Surface laptops and data center servers, out of China starting in 2026. The company has already moved much of its server production and requires 80% of server materials from outside China. Microsoft is also encouraging a shift in Xbox console production away from China, while Amazon Web Services is pursuing a non-China production strategy for AI data center servers.

title: Big Tech is driving the stock market to new records [Video] - AOL.com
summary: Big Tech companies, particularly those involved in artificial intelligence, are largely responsible for the S&P 500 reaching new record highs. The top 20 stocks by market cap in the index, encompassing major tech players like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Google, have significantly outperformed the broader index. Analysts believe that while the current focus is on AI infrastructure, the long-term market opportunity lies in companies effectively incorporating AI to improve their productivity and profitability.

title: Week in review: F5 data breach, Microsoft patches three actively exploited zero-days - Help Net Security
summary: This weekly review highlights significant cybersecurity news including an F5 data breach involving the theft of BIG-IP source code, and Microsoft patching three actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities. It also covers various other cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and cybersecurity developments in blockchain, AI, industrial control systems, and healthcare.

title: NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) Stock Rocketed Over 200% in 2023
summary: Polen Capital's "Polen Focus Growth Strategy" fund saw significant returns in 2023, with NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) being a key contributor as its stock rocketed over 200%. The article highlights NVIDIA's crucial role in the generative AI boom, providing the processing power for large language models and AI factories. NVIDIA was held by 180 hedge fund portfolios at the end of Q3 2023, up from 175 in the previous quarter.

title: Two New Windows Zero-Days Exploited in the Wild — One Affects Every Version Ever Shipped
summary: Microsoft has released fixes for 183 vulnerabilities, including two actively exploited Windows zero-days. One of these zero-days, CVE-2025-24990, affects every version of Windows ever shipped and allows local privilege escalation. The other, CVE-2025-59230, is the first zero-day exploit seen in RasMan.

title: Welcome to AI Week 2025
summary: Cloudflare announces "AI Week 2025," focusing on securing AI environments, protecting content creators from AI misuse, helping developers build secure AI experiences, and integrating AI to improve Cloudflare's own products. The company highlights the rapid pace of AI innovation and the critical need for robust security and control mechanisms to prevent data leaks, unauthorized usage, and content exploitation. Cloudflare aims to provide tools that allow organizations to leverage AI's benefits without sacrificing security or creators' intellectual property.

title: Why UnitedHealth (UNH) Stock Is Up Today
summary: UnitedHealth (UNH) shares rose 4.5% due to positive analyst actions and strategic company updates, including lifted price targets by Wolfe Research, Bernstein, and RBC Capital. The optimism stems from the belief that UnitedHealth can improve profit margins in its insurance division. This move follows a previous gain tied to hopes for an interest rate cut, though the stock is still significantly down year-to-date.

title: Agroz unveils AI-Powered farming system to boost production
